newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan gov't optimistic on Sidor sale approval.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan gov't optimistic on Sidor sale approval.

text.p: Venezuelan government officials and legislators from all parties said Wednesday they were confident a plan to privatize state steel company Sidor would secure approval from Congress.

"It's not going to be approved from one day to the next. We're prepared to give any additional information that is needed," Alberto Poletto, head of the government's privatization program told reporters in Congress.

Poletto presented the terms of the contract to privatize Sidor to Congress Wednesday. Under the contract, a controlling 70 percent stake will be sold to a consortium at auction. The remaining 30 percent will be held for later sale to workers, local companies and a possible public share issue.

Poletto said he sensed an atmosphere in Congress which recognized, "the need to sell basic industries which, if they are not sold, will collapse in the short term because neither the state nor the companies have the money to modernize technologically."
Congress President Cristobal Fernandez Dalo, who received the contract, said the sale of Sidor would be an important sign that Venezuela is opening up its economy.
Ramon Jose Medina, president of the special commission which will study the Sidor sale, said he was confident it would be approved before the end of ordinary Congressional sessions in early July.

Jorge Rig, head of the parliamentary faction of Radical Cause (Causa R) which has a strong participation in Sidor's unions, also said there was a mood of consensus in Congress to approve the Sidor sale.
Eleven companies have already qualified to bid for Sidor from Mexico, Brazil, Japan, South Korea, Argentina and Venezuela.
The 1.8 million tonne per year capacity company is considered Latin America's last remaining state-owned steel company.
